questions.text: Which ABG finding is most consistent with Type I (hypoxemic) respiratory failure?

questions.text: A patient is refractory hypoxemic — the PaO₂ does not improve significantly when FiO₂ is increased to 100%. Which mechanism best explains this?

answers.text: Intrapulmonary shunt — blood bypasses ventilated alveoli and cannot be oxygenated
V/Q mismatch — partial perfusion of poorly ventilated alveoli that responds to added oxygen
Diffusion impairment — oxygen cannot cross the thickened membrane
Decreased PiO₂ from high altitude

questions.text: A mechanically ventilated ARDS patient develops increased PIP and an increased Pplat. Both rise proportionally (delta unchanged). What is the most likely cause?

questions.text: Which control variable keeps pressure constant while allowing volume to vary?
